docs/guide-scope-guard.md:146:## Resolving violations
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:148:When `guard_session_check` detects forbidden writes:
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:150:1. **Remove the out-of-scope changes** — revert or delete the file(s) listed
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:152:2. **Or acknowledge a necessary expansion** — if the scope genuinely needs to
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:153:   widen, run `scope_contract_acknowledge` and then re-run `guard_session_check`.
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:154:3. Re-run `story_advance` once the session shows 0 violations.
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:156:Acknowledgement is not a silent pass. The acknowledged expansion remains warn
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:157:and reviewer-visible as a `scope.out_of_scope:<path>` row with `blocking=false`;
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:158:review, validation, and DONE gates still need their own evidence.
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:160:## Claude Code PreToolUse hook installation
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:162:The `PreToolUse` hook lets Claude Code intercept a tool call *before* it writes
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:163:a file.  Without it, the guard session can only detect violations after the fact.
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:168:lattice doctor
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:169:# look for: PreToolUse hook (Claude Code): installed (N hooks)
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:176:lattice doctor --format=json | jq '.guardSessions.preToolUseHook'
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:181:Add a `PreToolUse` entry to `.claude/settings.json` (create the file if absent):
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:188:        "matcher": "",
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:191:            "type": "command",
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:192:            "command": "node \"$(git -C \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\")/.claude/hooks/prewrite-scope-guard.cjs\""
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:201:> **Note:** A `prewrite-scope-guard.cjs` hook script is not yet shipped as a
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:202:> managed asset.  Until it is, the guard session provides watcher-fallback
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:203:> protection for all providers.  `lattice doctor` will report the hook as
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:204:> "not installed" and advise accordingly.  This is correct and expected during
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:205:> the current rollout phase.
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:207:### Managed asset drift
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:209:`lattice check` scans managed assets (CLAUDE.md, `.claude/hooks`, …) for drift.
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:210:Once the `prewrite-scope-guard.cjs` hook becomes a managed asset, `lattice check`
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:211:will report it as `MISSING` and `lattice check --apply` will install it.
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:213:## Watcher-fallback: what it means in practice
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:215:A `watcher-fallback` guard session still provides meaningful protection:
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:217:- Every `story_advance` re-checks the diff before allowing lifecycle progression.
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:218:- `guard_session_check` can be called manually at any point during DEV.
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:219:- Violations are recorded in the session and surfaced in `lattice doctor`.
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:220:- The lifecycle gate blocks if violations are present, regardless of mode.
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:222:The only thing `watcher-fallback` cannot do is prevent the forbidden file from
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:223:being written in the first place. For CI runners, Codex agents,
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:224:Antigravity/agy agents outside dispatch/pre-apply flow, and legacy Gemini
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:225:compatibility sessions, this is the expected and correct behavior — the gate
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:226:still catches the violation before the story moves to REVIEW.
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:230:A guard session requires a scope contract to check against.  If none exists,
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:231:`guard_session_check` clears any violations and returns a clean state — it never
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:232:fabricates violations from a missing contract.
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:235:# Set up a scope contract before starting a guard session
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:236:lattice scope_contract_set '{"storyId":"B-xxxx","mode":"enforce","allowedModify":["src/foo.ts"],...}'
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:237:# or derive one from the plan
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:238:lattice scope_contract_init_from_plan '{"storyId":"B-xxxx"}'
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:240:# Then start the guard session
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:241:lattice guard_session_start '{"storyId":"B-xxxx","provider":"claude-code"}'
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:244:See `docs/requirements/decisions/lifecycle-artifact-scope.md` for the scope
docs/guide-scope-guard.md:245:contract classifier policy.
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:1:# Step 3 handoff — Review-budget circuit breaker / stall adjudication (fixes class ②)
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:3:Audience: a fresh session picking this up cold. Self-contained. Parent program:
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:4:`docs/evidence-integrity-program-spec.md`. This is the second-priority failure
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:5:(runaway review rounds). Note: class ② is *caused* by class ① (each evidence-defect
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:6:fix invalidates the round and mints another), so Step 2 removes a large fraction of
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:7:these rounds; Step 3 is the backstop for the rest.
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:11:A story's review ballooned to 20+ rounds (the "S3" incident; the B-bf52 burn had 14
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:12:finding-bearing rounds / 46 review runs) with no effective brake. The deeper loss
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:13:was not the round count — it was taking **12 rounds to discover the task itself was
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:14:ill-posed** (F-058: CHK-003 was unreachable from the message text; the story ended
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:15:NOT DELIVERED), while F-059 shows plan.md claimed C2/C3/C4 delivered from round 4
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:16:onward and was never corrected. A numeric cap alone would not have surfaced the
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:17:unreachability; a forced adjudication point would.
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:19:## 2. What already exists (extend, do NOT rebuild)
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:21:Verified against real code:
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:24:  doc (lines ~3-8) describes the class-①→② livelock.
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:25:- `handlers/transition-effects.ts:284-289` — the stall detector is wrapped in a
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:26:  `try/catch` and is **advisory-only: it never blocks the transition**, it only
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:27:  appends text to output. This is the thing to harden.
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:30:  (`AUTO_RECOVERY_BUDGET = 1`), and is cleared by `story_resume --ack`. **14 review
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:31:  rounds passed under it** because it counts advances, not review rounds, and its
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:32:  threshold is 20. (See memory `b-bbaf-convergence-breaker-done`.)
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:34:So: a breaker exists but does not bite on review-round runaway. Extend the stall
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:35:detector into a blocking decision point; do not build a new breaker from scratch.
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:37:## 3. The fix — stall becomes a mandatory adjudication, not a warning
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:39:On stall trigger (≥ `STALL_MIN_ROUNDS` rounds, or N non-improving completed
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:40:rounds), **refuse to mint another ordinary review round** until one structured
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:41:action is recorded:
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:42:- a human authorizes continuation with a reason + a bounded additional budget; or
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:43:- the story is re-planned / split; or
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:44:- a root-cause / architecture escalation is recorded; or
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:45:- the blocking findings are explicitly resolved, disproven, deferred, or the scope
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:46:  is shrunk; or
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:47:- a checklist item is declared **unreachable** (the F-058 case — this is the option
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:48:  a raw cap would never surface).
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:50:Design notes:
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:51:- A raw absolute cap alone is too crude — the breaker should also consider whether
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:52:  blockers are decreasing, whether the same root cause recurs, and whether new
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:53:  material genuinely requires another round.
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:54:- BUT there must be a hard upper bound or a privileged override, so the advisory
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:55:  cannot be ignored indefinitely (today it is ignored — 20+ rounds).
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:56:- The real goal is to surface "are we converging, or is this task ill-posed?"
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:57:  **early**, and to force plan.md / claims to be reconciled with the authoritative
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:58:  evidence at that point (F-059).
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:60:## 4. The PreToolUse seatbelt (optional, the layer originally asked for)
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:61:Once the handler refuses to mint a new round past the threshold, a PreToolUse hook
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:62:can additionally warn/deny the "start another review round" action early (e.g.
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:63:`review_run_start`), before it runs — a seatbelt on top of the handler floor. Same
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:64:constraints as Step 2 §4: fail-open, advisory, both hosts, gate the Codex side on a
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:65:real-shell-tool-name e2e test.
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:68:- No story exceeds the configured review budget without a recorded escalation /
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:69:  override / unreachability declaration.
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:70:- On the third non-improving round, minting a fourth ordinary round is refused with
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:71:  a structured prompt for one of the §3 actions.
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:72:- A checklist item can be declared unreachable, which closes the loop instead of
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:73:  spinning (reproduce the F-058 scenario as the RED test).
docs/step3-review-budget-breaker-handoff.md:74:- The existing `convergence-breaker` and `story_resume --ack` paths still work and

docs/guide-hooks.md:1:# Proofbound Hooks Guide
docs/guide-hooks.md:3:Proofbound exposes 4 event points in every command's lifecycle and lets you configure shell hook commands in `lattice.config.json`. The design is inspired by Claude Code's PreToolUse / PostToolUse / SessionStart / Stop mechanism, and its goal is to decouple "things the agent wants to do after a command finishes" from the Proofbound framework core.
docs/guide-hooks.md:7:Proofbound initialization merges a Claude Code `UserPromptSubmit` hook into `.claude/settings.json`:
docs/guide-hooks.md:14:        "matcher": "",
docs/guide-hooks.md:17:            "type": "command",
docs/guide-hooks.md:18:            "command": "node \"$(git -C \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\")/.claude/hooks/session-brief-reminder.cjs\""
docs/guide-hooks.md:27:This hook is only a soft reminder: it locates the repository from the hook JSON's `cwd`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, or the current cwd, reads the legacy `.lattice/activity.jsonl` mirror, `docs/story/activity.jsonl`, and the story-scoped `docs/story/actives/*/activity.jsonl`, and looks for the most recent `session_brief` heartbeat. By default, anything within 60 minutes is treated as fresh and the hook stays silent; when the most recent heartbeat is older than 60 minutes or there is no fresh record, it prints:
docs/guide-hooks.md:29:```text
docs/guide-hooks.md:30:Run lattice session_brief first to restore context
docs/guide-hooks.md:33:The threshold can be adjusted with `LATTICE_SESSION_BRIEF_FRESH_MINUTES`. Malformed stdin, a missing activity file, and single-line parse failures all exit zero and must never block the user's prompt. Claude Code hooks/settings belong only to `.claude/`; Proofbound init does not create `.lattice-codex/hooks` or `.lattice-codex/settings.json`.
docs/guide-hooks.md:37:- After the agent runs `story_advance phase=DEV`, automatically run `git fetch origin main && git merge`
docs/guide-hooks.md:38:- When a command errors, push the error log to Slack / WeCom / Telegram
docs/guide-hooks.md:39:- Observer-style tools that want real-time notifications when the Proofbound state changes (more elegant than polling activity.jsonl)
docs/guide-hooks.md:40:- Automatically back up the fixture directory before entering the TEST phase

docs/guide-hooks.md:45:Add a `hooks` field to `lattice.config.json`:

docs/guide-hooks.md:57:      "*": ["./scripts/log-result.sh"]

docs/guide-hooks.md:71:Each stage is a `Record<string, string[]>`: the key is the match condition, and the value is an array of shell commands (run serially in array order).
docs/guide-hooks.md:75:| Stage | Trigger timing | Key match rule |
docs/guide-hooks.md:77:| `preCommand` | Before the handler runs (arguments already parsed, phase gate already passed) | `commandName` or `"*"` |
docs/guide-hooks.md:78:| `postCommand` | After the handler returns successfully, before `process.exit(0)` | `commandName` or `"*"` |
docs/guide-hooks.md:79:| `onError` | After the handler throws, before `process.exit(1)` | `commandName` or `"*"` |
docs/guide-hooks.md:80:| `onPhaseChange` | After `story_advance` persists the new phase | The literal `"FROM->TO"` or `"*"` |
docs/guide-hooks.md:82:**Exact match + the `"*"` wildcard both run**—this is not a fallback. For example, with `preCommand: { "story_advance": [...], "*": [...] }`, running `story_advance` runs both groups serially (the exact match first, then the wildcard).
docs/guide-hooks.md:86:Each hook command receives the full `process.env` through `child_process.spawn`, plus the injected `LATTICE_*` environment variable names listed below:
docs/guide-hooks.md:90:| `LATTICE_STAGE` | all | legacy env var; the current Proofbound stage name (`preCommand`/`postCommand`/`onError`/`onPhaseChange`) |
docs/guide-hooks.md:91:| `LATTICE_COMMAND` | all | legacy env var; the current Proofbound command name (e.g. `story_advance`) |
docs/guide-hooks.md:92:| `LATTICE_CWD` | all | legacy env var; the process cwd when the hook fired |
docs/guide-hooks.md:93:| `LATTICE_ROOT` | all | legacy env var; the current Proofbound project root (after `--root` resolution) |
docs/guide-hooks.md:94:| `LATTICE_ARGS_JSON` | preCommand / postCommand / onError | legacy env var; the argument JSON passed to the handler (truncated to 8KB) |
docs/guide-hooks.md:95:| `LATTICE_RESULT_JSON` | postCommand | legacy env var; the handler return value JSON (truncated to 8KB) |
docs/guide-hooks.md:96:| `LATTICE_ERROR` | onError | legacy env var; the error.message string |
docs/guide-hooks.md:97:| `LATTICE_STORY_ID` | onPhaseChange + any stage when an active story exists | legacy env var; the current Proofbound story id (`B-xxxx`) |
docs/guide-hooks.md:98:| `LATTICE_PHASE` | any stage when an active story exists | legacy env var; the current phase (at the time the hook runs) |
docs/guide-hooks.md:99:| `LATTICE_OLD_PHASE` | onPhaseChange | legacy env var; the phase before the transition |
docs/guide-hooks.md:100:| `LATTICE_NEW_PHASE` | onPhaseChange | legacy env var; the phase after the transition |
docs/guide-hooks.md:104:1. **Non-blocking failure**: a hook exiting non-zero, throwing, or not being found never blocks the main command. It prints a `[lattice-hook] failed (exit N): <stage> <cmd>` warning to stderr and appends a `category=hook:exec` health issue to the legacy runtime health path `~/.lattice/health.jsonl`.
docs/guide-hooks.md:105:2. **30-second timeout**: each hook command is timed independently and receives `SIGKILL` after 30 seconds. It prints `[lattice-hook] timeout (30s): ...` to stderr, with health category `hook:timeout`.
docs/guide-hooks.md:106:3. **stdout limit**: a hook's stdout is echoed to stderr only for the first 200 characters, to avoid polluting the main command's JSON output (this matters most for postCommand: an agent piping into jq does not want hook notes mixed into the JSON).
docs/guide-hooks.md:107:4. **Sequential execution**: commands within the same stage are awaited serially in array order, each one waiting for the previous to finish. preCommand fully completes before the handler runs; postCommand fully completes before `process.exit(0)`.
docs/guide-hooks.md:108:5. **Concurrency**: exact-match + wildcard commands also run in order—the exact match runs to completion first, then the wildcard.
docs/guide-hooks.md:109:6. **Environment variable truncation**: both `LATTICE_RESULT_JSON` and `LATTICE_ARGS_JSON` are truncated to 8KB to prevent blowing up the env (the default ARG_MAX on macOS / Linux is roughly 256KB; Windows is far stricter).
docs/guide-hooks.md:110:7. **stage validation**: an invalid stage key under `hooks` is silently ignored (PROBE class, no health written).
docs/guide-hooks.md:114:### Example 1: Automatically rebase from main on every `story_advance`
docs/guide-hooks.md:120:      "story_advance": [
docs/guide-hooks.md:121:        "git fetch origin main >/dev/null 2>&1 && git merge --no-edit origin/main || true"
docs/guide-hooks.md:128:This is hooked into preCommand rather than postCommand because merging after the advance could produce conflicts the agent cannot see. A failing preCommand does not block either, but it at least surfaces the conflict in the Proofbound command's stderr.
docs/guide-hooks.md:130:### Example 2: Trigger a Telegram notification on onPhaseChange
docs/guide-hooks.md:137:        "curl -s -XPOST \"https://api.telegram.org/bot$TG_BOT_TOKEN/sendMessage\" -d chat_id=$TG_CHAT_ID -d text=\"lattice $LATTICE_STORY_ID: $LATTICE_OLD_PHASE→$LATTICE_NEW_PHASE\""
docs/guide-hooks.md:144:`TG_BOT_TOKEN` / `TG_CHAT_ID` are inherited through the shell environment (the hook's env is derived from `process.env`).
docs/guide-hooks.md:146:### Example 3: Snapshot the fixture directory before entering TEST
docs/guide-hooks.md:153:        "tar czf /tmp/lattice-fixtures-$LATTICE_STORY_ID.tgz tests/fixtures/"
docs/guide-hooks.md:160:When `test_auto` finishes, it runs `git restore + git clean -fd` on the fixturesDir; should broken code cause the fixtures to be lost, this tar archive is the last-resort backup.
docs/guide-hooks.md:162:### Example 4: Push errors to a webhook
docs/guide-hooks.md:169:        "curl -s -XPOST $WEBHOOK_URL -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d \"{\\\"command\\\":\\\"$LATTICE_COMMAND\\\",\\\"error\\\":\\\"$(echo $LATTICE_ERROR | head -c 200)\\\"}\""
docs/guide-hooks.md:176:Mind the shell escaping—this is fine for simple cases, but for anything complex wrap it in a standalone shell script and write `["./scripts/push-error.sh"]` in the hook, reading the env from inside the script.
docs/guide-hooks.md:180:- Hook didn't fire? Run `lattice doctor` and check `health.jsonl` for `hook:exec` / `hook:timeout` / `hook:resolve` entries
docs/guide-hooks.md:181:- Hook didn't receive the environment variables? Prepend `env | sort > /tmp/lattice-env-debug.txt` to the hook command
docs/guide-hooks.md:182:- Hook output polluting the main command? Check whether stdout returned a non-empty string—postCommand should write logs to a file rather than stdout
docs/guide-hooks.md:186:- **Synchronous blocking hooks**: all stages are fire-and-await, but a failure never aborts the main command. If you need "hook fail → block the main command" semantics, `kill -9` the parent process yourself from inside the script (not recommended; the behavior is counterintuitive).
docs/guide-hooks.md:187:- **Cross-command state sharing**: each hook is spawned independently and shares no stdout/state with the others. If you need it, write a file or pass it through environment variables.
docs/guide-hooks.md:188:- **Cancelling the main command**: an onError hook already runs after the main command has failed, so it cannot be used to "retry" the main command. To retry, the agent calls it again itself.
docs/guide-hooks.md:190:## Cooperation with the Stale-detector
docs/guide-hooks.md:192:`lattice doctor` now also aggregates `hook:*` health issues, which together with the `stale-detector`'s stderr warnings form Proofbound's "self-observation" system:
docs/guide-hooks.md:194:- stale-detector: proactively prints soft reminders before each command runs (phase stuck / item stuck in_progress / idle lattice / open bug overdue)
docs/guide-hooks.md:195:- hook: spawns user scripts at event points, leaving a trail in the legacy runtime health path `~/.lattice/health.jsonl`
docs/guide-hooks.md:196:- doctor: aggregates the health status of both
docs/guide-hooks.md:198:See `core/stale-detector.ts` and `core/hooks.ts` for details.

docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:1:# Quorum Duplicate-Guard: downgrade-aware fix — Design Spec (rev 3, draft)
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:3:Status: DRAFT for review · Date: 2026-07-25 · Author: jek + Claude (brainstorming)
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:4:Supersedes: rev 1 (PreToolUse-as-gate) and rev 2 (per-story lock + atomic critical
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:5:section) — both retracted after two rounds of cross-host audit (Codex + Agy).
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:7:## 0. Why rev 3 (what two audit rounds established)
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:9:- Rev 1 (PreToolUse hook + CLI pre-check): a hook cannot enforce (fail-open, sees a
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:10:  raw Bash program not argv, trivially evaded), and a pre-check before the handler
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:12:- Rev 2 (per-story lock + atomic critical section): direction affirmed, but it
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:14:  in doing so introduced new blockers — AB/BA lock-ordering vs `main-write-lock`,
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:15:  a sync→async handler-contract change, a fail-closed path with no ledger-recovery
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:16:  story, and a cross-host mutual-exclusion guarantee a filesystem lock cannot give.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:18:- **The real burn (S3) was same-host, sequential re-submission after a `main`
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:19:  merge — not concurrent racing.** Root cause: the duplicate guard keys on the raw
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:20:  material digest, while the floor accepts the prior verdict via
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:21:  `eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade` (stable `storyFilesHash`). A merge that
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:22:  changes material but not `storyFilesHash` lands in the gap: the prior verdict is
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:23:  no longer "same material" to the duplicate guard, so a second quorum is appended.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:25:Rev 3 fixes exactly that gap and nothing more.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:29:Make `quorum_submit`'s existing duplicate-runId guard **downgrade-aware**, so a
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:30:re-submission of a round whose verdict is already recorded — and still accepted by
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:31:the floor via `storyFilesHash` downgrade — is recognized as a duplicate and
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:32:refused. Reuse the existing exact-byte transaction + HEAD CAS for atomicity. No new
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:33:lock, no async-contract change, no cross-host claims.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:35:Explicit non-goals: concurrent multi-host mutual exclusion; guarding
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:36:`autopilot_review_submit` / `story_advance` / `verification_evidence_add`; any
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:37:PreToolUse hook; any general "quorum-evidence idempotency" claim.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:39:## 2. The fix
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:41:In `handlers/quorum-submit.ts`, the duplicate guard (currently ~lines 474–490)
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:42:reads committed `host_verdict` events and refuses if one exists for a planned
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:43:runId (`${storyId}-q-r${round}`) **at the same `materialDigest`**.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:45:Change: before comparing, pass the committed events through
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:46:`eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade(events, currentMaterialHash,
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:47:currentStoryFilesHash, advisories)` (`core/review-escalation.ts:948`) — the same
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:48:helper the floor uses. This rewrites the `materialDigest` of prior verdicts whose
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:49:`storyFilesHash` matches the current one to the current material digest. The
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:50:existing runId duplicate check then sees the post-merge prior verdict as current
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:51:and refuses the redundant re-submit.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:53:Semantics stay narrow and correct: the criterion is **"a verdict for this exact
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:54:runId already exists (after downgrade)"**, NOT "the floor is satisfied". A
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:55:genuinely new round (`round+1`, different runId) has no matching prior verdict and
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:56:is never refused — so an escalation that still needs another quorum is unaffected.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:57:This is deliberately the opposite of rev 2 §4, whose floor-satisfaction shortcut
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:58:would have falsely refused needed submissions (audit blocker).
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:60:### Single source of truth
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:61:The downgrade helper is the one the floor already consumes; using it here makes the
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:62:duplicate guard and the floor agree by construction. The gap that produced S3 was
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:65:## 3. Atomicity — reuse what exists, add one cheap revalidation
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:67:No new lock. The existing `commitLifecycleMetadataTransaction` already performs a
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:68:HEAD `update-ref` CAS, which aborts if HEAD moved under the operation — sufficient
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:69:for the sequential same-host case that burned us.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:71:Optional hardening (small, in the same handler): immediately before the commit,
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:72:re-derive `currentMaterialHash` / `currentStoryFilesHash` and re-run the
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:73:downgrade-aware duplicate check against freshly-read committed events. This closes
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:74:the narrow window where an *uncommitted/untracked* change (which leaves HEAD
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:75:unchanged, so the CAS does not catch it) drifts material between the initial check
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:76:and the commit. Marked optional so the core change stays minimal; include if the
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:81:If the downgrade-aware evaluation cannot run (unreadable/parse-failed events), fall
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:82:back to the **current** raw-digest duplicate check (today's behavior) and proceed.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:83:This introduces no new hard-fail path, so it needs no process-events recovery story
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:84:and cannot strand an escalation-required story — sidestepping the rev 2 fail-closed
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:85:blocker. The fix only ever makes the existing check *smarter*, never *stricter in a
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:86:way that can brick the workflow*.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:88:## 5. Known residuals (explicitly NOT closed)
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:90:State these in code comments and the story so no false "idempotent" claim is made:
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:92:- **Concurrent multi-host racing** is not closed. Two independent checkouts have no
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:93:  shared lock; the existing exact-byte transaction + HEAD CAS give best-effort
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:94:  protection only. Out of scope by design (a filesystem lock cannot provide it).
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:95:- **`autopilot_review_submit`** ordinary path writes the same `host_verdict`
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:96:  evidence and can still append a redundant single verdict after a merge — the same
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:97:  class, deferred. A fast-follow can reuse this same downgrade-aware check on that
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:98:  path.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:99:- No claim of general quorum-evidence idempotency; this fixes one specific
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:100:  duplicate-runId gap.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:104:- **S3 repro (RED):** set up a satisfied round; apply a `main` merge that changes
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:105:  material but leaves `storyFilesHash` stable; re-run `quorum_submit` for the same
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:106:  round. Assert current code appends a redundant quorum; assert the downgrade-aware
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:107:  guard refuses it after the fix.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:108:- **No false refusal (regression guard for the rev-2 blocker):** a story where
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:109:  escalation legitimately requires a further round — assert the new guard does NOT
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:110:  refuse the needed, distinct-runId submission.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:111:- **Fallback:** corrupt/unreadable events → guard degrades to raw-digest behavior,
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:112:  no throw, no strand.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:113:- (If §3 optional hardening is included) **uncommitted-drift window:** mutate
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:114:  material without moving HEAD between check and commit; assert the pre-commit
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:115:  revalidation refuses.
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:117:## 7. Implementation path
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:119:Lands through a Lattice story (audit trail), not a direct commit to `main`. It
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:120:touches the `quorum_submit` guard, so it is a high-assurance change and should go
docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md:121:through full cross-host quorum review itself — dogfooding the very command it fixes.

docs/guide.md:140:## Host Overflow
docs/guide.md:142:Proofbound Host Overflow is a **manual-first** bounded overflow process: Proofbound holds story, scope, receipt review, and merge responsibility, and Claude Code is only an execution host, not a release-readiness oracle.
docs/guide.md:144:Recommended order:
docs/guide.md:147:lattice host_status --host=claude-code --json
docs/guide.md:148:lattice handoff_create --storyId=B-xxxx --fromHost=codex --toHost=claude-code --json
docs/guide.md:149:lattice handoff_worktree_create --file=handoff-pack.json --json
docs/guide.md:150:lattice host_dispatch --host=claude-code --file=handoff-pack.json --mode=supervised --json
docs/guide.md:151:lattice handoff_receipt_submit --file=receipt.json --json
docs/guide.md:156:- `host_status` only reports overflow readiness; it does not grant authority.
docs/guide.md:157:- `handoff_create` produces a bounded pack containing `packId`, `packHash`, `baseSha`, `allowedPaths`, `deniedPaths`, required commands, and execution instructions.
docs/guide.md:158:- `handoff_worktree_create` only projects worktree/branch/cleanup guidance; it does not automatically create, merge, clean up, or trust results.
docs/guide.md:159:- `host_dispatch` only returns `planned|unavailable` and `nextAction`; it does not auto-trust, submit evidence, verify receipts, or widen local assurance.
docs/guide.md:160:- `handoff_receipt_submit` only accepts a local diagnostic receipt; even on `accepted-local`, it remains diagnostic until matching local assurance evidence exists.
docs/guide.md:162:The later `dispatch_plan` / `dispatch_prepare` / `dispatch_run` must also obey the same boundary:
docs/guide.md:164:- They may only perform supervised, visible automation. The operator must be able to see the target host, the plan, the receipt, the status, and the review/merge guidance.
docs/guide.md:165:- If the target host lacks the corresponding CLI/runtime, the result must degrade to `unavailable` or a diagnostic `nextAction`; it must not silently switch to another host or skip silently.
docs/guide.md:166:- Even a fake/local receipt may not auto-merge, may not verify a receipt bundle, and may not widen local assurance.
docs/guide.md:168:For the detailed architecture, see [`requirements/decisions/host-overflow.md`](requirements/decisions/host-overflow.md).

docs/guide.md:196:### Unattended dispatch — `dispatch_auto` (policy-authorized)
docs/guide.md:198:`dispatch_auto` is the **policy-authorized unattended scheduler**, an extension path of `overflow_auto`. How it differs from `overflow_auto`:
docs/guide.md:200:| | `overflow_auto` | `dispatch_auto` |
docs/guide.md:202:| Default mode | suggest-only (requires `--approve --start` to actually start) | policy-gated (starts workers automatically once checks pass) |
docs/guide.md:203:| Policy required | No | Yes (refuses if the policy is missing or unauthorized) |
docs/guide.md:204:| Host safety check | No | Yes (refuses if `unattendedSafe=false`) |
docs/guide.md:205:| Unattended | No | Yes |
docs/guide.md:207:If you are already using `overflow_auto` and want unattended workers, first define a dispatch policy and then migrate to `dispatch_auto`. The `overflow_auto` `nextAction` field will point to `dispatch_auto`.

docs/guide.md:216:  --network=none --commandAllowlist='node -e "process.exit(0)"' \

docs/guide.md:243:**Unattended mode remains user-authorized and local-assurance-safe:**
docs/guide.md:245:- `dispatch_auto` **refuses** (explicitly, without pretending to execute) in the following cases:
docs/guide.md:247:  - the policy does not exist or is unauthorized (`authorized=false`)
docs/guide.md:248:  - the host is unavailable (`status=unavailable`) or `unattendedSafe=false`
docs/guide.md:249:  - the host is not in the policy's `allowedHosts` list
docs/guide.md:251:- Worker output is only an evidence candidate; it does not constitute gate proof.

docs/guide.md:254:  and review-quorum evidence make it locally admissible.
docs/guide.md:256:## Combining Code and Documentation
docs/guide.md:258:When code is generated, the documentation for that code must be generated in sync, in JSON format. Every time the code is modified, the code's documentation must be updated in sync, down to every Class and function. A Class's documentation is fixed once set, but a function's documentation must be updated every time. The purpose of this is to extract the project's overall state in real time, to make it easy to analyze task completion, to tie it back to source material, and to keep it dynamically and promptly updated. Where each piece of code's requirement came from, how many times it has been updated, and the content of each update should all be recorded; deleted or deprecated code should not be removed either—all history must be preserved. Much of this content is subjective and needs to be validated with automated scripts.
docs/guide.md:262:This includes white-box and black-box tests. Every test needs detailed tracking: time, content, a test code reference (`{featureId}-{name}`), whether it is verified, and the verification result.
docs/guide.md:264:## Use MCP to invoke scripts; do not let the LLM call a script directly—it must be written as an MCP service, otherwise the service becomes very hard to use.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:1:# Decision: gate milestone `not_applicable` behind an auditable justification
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:3:- Story: B-f7b3 (milestone-observability hardening), checklist item CHK-007
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:4:- Status: decided
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:5:- Closes: findings M4 caveat (zero-evidence self-exemption via `not_applicable`)
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:9:`normalizeMilestone` in `packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts` validates a
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:10:milestone `status` against `VALID_MILESTONE_STATUSES` only. Any row can be written with
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:11:`status: 'not_applicable'` with no rule asserting the row is genuinely inapplicable.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:12:That status then:
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:14:- short-circuits the uncovered-required-milestone gate check in
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:15:  `evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence` (in `proofstory.ts`, which skips `not_applicable` rows
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:16:  from the uncovered-required check), and
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:17:- is treated as `complete` and rendered in the completed group by the milestone-status
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:18:  report (`packages/main/src/core/milestone-status.ts`).
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:20:So `not_applicable` is a **zero-evidence self-exemption**: an agent can silently exempt a
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:21:required milestone from DONE-intent-equivalence with no auditable reason and no human record.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:25:Require an auditable `notApplicableDecision` on every `not_applicable` milestone row,
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:26:mirroring the existing, already-shipped precedent for parent-roadmap rows
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:27:(`packages/main/src/core/parent-roadmap-totality.ts`: `ParentRoadmapNotApplicableDecision`
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:28:+ `validNotApplicable`).
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:30:The decision operates at **two altitudes**: a structural field on the row, plus a
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:31:DONE-gate policy diagnostic. It is deliberately **not** a hard throw on absence — an
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:32:absent decision is a diagnostic gap, so the read/build path never throws for a
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:33:missing (only a *malformed present*) decision.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:35:New shared field on `MilestoneLedgerItem` (`packages/main/src/core/types.ts`):
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:38:export interface MilestoneNotApplicableDecision {
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:40:  decidedBy: string;  // human / agent identity of record
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:41:  decidedAt: string;  // ISO timestamp
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:50:   is **optional**. When the field is **present** it must be an object with non-empty
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:51:   `reason`, `decidedBy`, and `decidedAt`; a malformed present shape throws a structural
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:52:   error (via `normalizeNotApplicableDecision`). When the field is **absent** it is left
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:53:   off the row and **nothing is thrown** — for any status, including `not_applicable`.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:54:   This keeps existing ledgers readable and makes the policy (below) the single place a
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:55:   missing exemption is surfaced.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:56:2. **Hash backward-compatibility.** `notApplicableDecision` is attached to the row object
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:57:   **only when present**, so a row without a decision keeps the exact same object shape —
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:58:   and therefore the exact same `computeMilestoneLedgerHash` output — as before this field
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:59:   existed. Existing confirmed ledgers (e.g. B-f7b3's own
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:60:   `sha256:68173e86…`) remain valid and unchanged. When a decision *is* present it
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:61:   participates in the hash like every other row field, so changing a justification changes
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:62:   the ledger hash and drops a `confirmed` ledger back to `candidate` (existing behavior in
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:63:   `buildMilestoneLedger`) — the exemption cannot be back-edited under a frozen confirmed
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:64:   ledger without re-confirmation.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:65:3. **Policy (DONE-gate altitude).** In `evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence`, a `not_applicable`
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:66:   row still self-exempts from the uncovered-required-milestone set, but a row that lacks a
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:67:   **valid** `notApplicableDecision` (checked by `validMilestoneNotApplicable`) emits a
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:68:   `not_applicable_missing_decision` diagnostic gap (severity `fail`). Under `enforce` mode
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:69:   this blocks DONE. This is where an unjustified exemption is caught — a diagnostic gap,
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:70:   never a hard throw in the read path.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:72:## Contract preservation (explicitly not weakened)
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:74:- **PLAN-only write path**: the field is set through the same `milestone_ledger_add` /
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:75:  `buildMilestoneLedger` PLAN-phase path; no new write surface, no runtime/DONE-phase write.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:76:- **Hash-bound**: field participates in `computeMilestoneLedgerHash`; confirmed→candidate
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:78:- **Intent-collision-confirmed**: `acceptedIntentBinding` is retained only while
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:79:  `existingHash === ledgerHash` (in `confirmMilestoneLedger`); adding/altering a justification changes the hash and
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:80:  therefore requires re-binding, exactly as for any other row edit.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:82:## Rejected alternatives
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:84:- **Free-form policy flag with no fields** — rejected: still zero-evidence; nothing to audit.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:85:- **Human-only approval (approvedBy/approvedAt/revisitTrigger like `deferral`)** — heavier
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:86:  than needed for CHK-007; the parent-roadmap `notApplicableDecision` triad
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:87:  (reason/decidedBy/decidedAt) is the established, lighter precedent and is sufficient to
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:88:  remove the self-exemption. Revisit if a human-gate requirement is later added.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:89:- **Reason on a separate side-file** — rejected: would not be hash-bound to the row and could
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:90:  drift from the ledger.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:92:## Backward compatibility
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:94:Existing ledgers stay readable. Because the field is optional at normalize time and is only
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:95:attached to the row when present, a ledger with `not_applicable` rows that carry **no**
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:96:decision still parses and — critically — hashes **identically** to before this change (a row
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:97:without the field is byte-for-byte the same object it was, so `computeMilestoneLedgerHash` is
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:98:unchanged). Confirmed ledgers such as B-f7b3's
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:99:`sha256:68173e86acd0f275fc8788a7ee1f577a5446e922904285147db66aeed7fd5c8e` remain valid.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:101:The unjustified exemptions this item closes are surfaced not as a read-path throw but as a
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:102:DONE-gate `not_applicable_missing_decision` diagnostic gap (severity `fail`, blocking under
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:103:`enforce`). Migration for an author who wants such a row to pass DONE = add the justification
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:104:triad (`reason` / `decidedBy` / `decidedAt`) to each such row; doing so changes the ledger
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md:105:hash and requires re-confirmation, exactly as for any other row edit.

docs/host-run-usage.md:18:desktop sessions all burned real tokens that the ledger never recorded. Every

docs/host-run-usage.md:81:Only a **bounded** amount of state is retained for usage parsing — the last
docs/host-run-usage.md:82:usage-bearing line (codex `turn.completed` / the claude `result` envelope),
docs/host-run-usage.md:83:capped at 1 MiB per line. A line over the cap is dropped (not retained), so a
docs/host-run-usage.md:84:flooding host can never exhaust memory or manufacture a count. Truncation
docs/host-run-usage.md:85:poisoning is tracked **relative to the retained usage candidate**: when a drop
docs/host-run-usage.md:86:happens **after** the retained usage line — or no usage line was ever
docs/host-run-usage.md:87:retained — the dropped line may have carried the real final numbers, so the
docs/host-run-usage.md:88:usage final records `unavailable` (reason `usage_line_retention_truncated`)
docs/host-run-usage.md:89:rather than a fabricated **or stale** value. A drop **followed by** a later
docs/host-run-usage.md:90:valid usage-bearing line does not poison the run: last-usage-wins makes the
docs/host-run-usage.md:91:later retained line the freshest usage information, so it is recorded honestly
docs/host-run-usage.md:92:(e.g. one huge non-usage output line early in the stream no longer discards a
docs/host-run-usage.md:93:perfectly good final usage event).
docs/host-run-usage.md:95:### Passthrough routing (text vs `--json`)
docs/host-run-usage.md:97:| Mode | Host stdout | Host stderr | Process stdout carries |
docs/host-run-usage.md:99:| text (default) | streamed live to **process.stdout** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | the live host stdout (the handler does not re-print it — no double-print) |
docs/host-run-usage.md:100:| `--json` | streamed live to **process.stderr** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | ONLY the single JSON result line (kept clean) |
docs/host-run-usage.md:102:In `--json` mode the bounded host transcript (at most 8 MiB per managed run) is
docs/host-run-usage.md:103:delivered live on **stderr** so that **stdout stays clean** for the one JSON
docs/host-run-usage.md:104:result. If the transcript exceeds that ceiling, the JSON result reports
docs/host-run-usage.md:105:`truncated=true` and does not promise the omitted tail; the JSON `stdout` field
docs/host-run-usage.md:106:carries only the bounded usage-parse tail, not an unbounded or complete
docs/host-run-usage.md:109:If the live passthrough sink fails mid-run, delivery stops at the first failure
docs/host-run-usage.md:110:but the run, usage recording, and slot release still complete: text mode prints a
docs/host-run-usage.md:111:`host_run warning:` line to stderr and the `--json` result carries a non-null
docs/host-run-usage.md:112:`passthroughError` field. This holds for **both** failure shapes a closed
docs/host-run-usage.md:113:downstream pipe can take: a **synchronous** write throw, and — because Node
docs/host-run-usage.md:114:delivers pipe write failures like a real `EPIPE` as an **asynchronous `'error'`
docs/host-run-usage.md:115:event** on `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` rather than a throw — that async
docs/host-run-usage.md:116:stream error too. `host_run` attaches (and, in a `finally`, removes) its own
docs/host-run-usage.md:117:stdout/stderr `'error'` listeners for the duration of the run, so a real EPIPE is
docs/host-run-usage.md:118:contained into the same `passthroughError` state instead of crashing the process;
docs/host-run-usage.md:119:once a stream is known broken, the best-effort diagnostic writes to it are
docs/host-run-usage.md:120:skipped rather than risk a late unhandled `'error'`, and **every** live
docs/host-run-usage.md:121:passthrough chunk write *and* final diagnostic write is settle-aware:
docs/host-run-usage.md:122:outstanding writes are tracked with a shared pending counter (throughput is never
docs/host-run-usage.md:123:serialized) that the `finally` **drains before removing the listeners** — bounded
docs/host-run-usage.md:124:by a defensive ~2s cap so a pathologically wedged stream can never hang the
docs/host-run-usage.md:125:command — so a late EPIPE from the FINAL live stdout chunk of a text-mode run, or
docs/host-run-usage.md:126:from the FIRST stderr write of a quiet run (which never tripped the skip), still
docs/host-run-usage.md:127:fires while a listener is attached.
docs/host-run-usage.md:129:Exactly one of `--prompt` / `--promptFile` is required for ordinary managed
docs/host-run-usage.md:130:runs. Formal cross-provider reviewer mode is the exception: `--managedReview`
docs/host-run-usage.md:131:forbids both and derives the exact prompt from the signed ReviewRun. A host
docs/host-run-usage.md:132:non-zero exit (or a cap refusal) propagates as a non-zero process exit; in
docs/host-run-usage.md:133:`--json` mode `exitCode` is a field.
docs/host-run-usage.md:135:### Reviewer launch
docs/host-run-usage.md:137:Native direct `review_pass_set` / reviewer `finding_add` is formal evidence only
docs/host-run-usage.md:138:when the exact tool invocation carries a short-lived Ed25519 attestation from a
docs/host-run-usage.md:139:registered host-adapter broker. The signed claims bind the Story, agent and
docs/host-run-usage.md:140:lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch prompt/binding, adapter and host
docs/host-run-usage.md:141:identity, and an invocation nonce. Lattice stores only the broker public-key
docs/host-run-usage.md:142:registration; it has no issuer command and does not keep the broker private key
docs/host-run-usage.md:143:in the repository or `.lattice` runtime state. The adapter injects the signed
docs/host-run-usage.md:144:attestation over a dedicated inherited descriptor for that exact Lattice CLI
docs/host-run-usage.md:145:process. Inline environment tokens are not accepted.
docs/host-run-usage.md:147:An adapter integration must therefore do both parts: register its public key in
docs/host-run-usage.md:148:`nativeReviewInvocation.brokers`, then sign and descriptor-inject each exact
docs/host-run-usage.md:149:review closeout invocation from its authenticated host tool-execution seam. If
docs/host-run-usage.md:150:the current Codex/Claude host does not provide that broker integration, native
docs/host-run-usage.md:151:direct evidence fails closed and is advisory-only; use the managed reviewer flow
docs/host-run-usage.md:152:below for formal evidence. `dispatch` and `review_run_start` do not issue this
docs/host-run-usage.md:153:capability, and a raw provider CLI cannot promote a self-generated key into the
docs/host-run-usage.md:154:registered broker set.
docs/host-run-usage.md:156:The attestation nonce is atomically consumed once to prevent replay. That local
docs/host-run-usage.md:158:ancestry is corroboration rather than required authority: an unavailable `ps`
docs/host-run-usage.md:159:view does not reject a valid broker attestation, but any observable mixed
docs/host-run-usage.md:160:Codex/Claude ancestry rejects direct evidence even when the nearest provider
docs/host-run-usage.md:161:matches. A same-UID/root attacker that can replace trusted configuration or
docs/host-run-usage.md:162:instrument the broker is outside this local assurance boundary.

docs/host-run-usage.md:267:Every usage row carries the attribution passed to `host_run`:
docs/host-run-usage.md:269:| Argument | Ledger field | Notes |

docs/host-run-usage.md:273:| `--phase` | `phase` | When omitted and `--storyId` is set, the phase resolves from the **configured story store** at call time (honoring a project's `storyDir`); an explicit `--phase` is used as-is and the store is never read. |

docs/host-run-usage.md:277:`--reviewRunId` must start with `<storyId>:` when `--storyId` is given, so a
docs/host-run-usage.md:278:ledger row can never silently mis-join across stories — a mismatch is refused
docs/host-run-usage.md:279:before any host is spawned. Omitting `--reviewRunId` / `--lane` leaves
docs/host-run-usage.md:280:`threadId` / `subagentId` null (no empty-string pollution).
docs/host-run-usage.md:282:When `--storyId` is given **without** `--phase`, the phase is resolved through the
docs/host-run-usage.md:283:configured story store; a story unknown to that store is refused pre-spawn. When
docs/host-run-usage.md:284:`--phase` is supplied the store is never consulted, so `--phase` works with or
docs/host-run-usage.md:285:without `--storyId` even in a project whose story metadata lives under a
docs/host-run-usage.md:286:custom `storyDir`.
docs/host-run-usage.md:288:## Per-host usage semantics
docs/host-run-usage.md:290:Provider truth is preferred over estimates; an absence is recorded as an explicit
docs/host-run-usage.md:291:`source=unavailable`, never a fabricated zero.
docs/host-run-usage.md:293:- **codex** — parses the terminal `turn.completed` usage event from
docs/host-run-usage.md:294:  `codex exec --json` and maps it to `{ input: input_tokens - cached_input_tokens,
docs/host-run-usage.md:295:  cacheRead: cached_input_tokens, cacheCreation: null, output: output_tokens }`.
docs/host-run-usage.md:296:  The `input` field is the **uncached remainder** (codex `input_tokens` includes
docs/host-run-usage.md:297:  cached input); the original payload (including `reasoning_output_tokens`) is
docs/host-run-usage.md:298:  digested raw.
docs/host-run-usage.md:299:- **claude** — parses the stream-json `result` envelope usage via
docs/host-run-usage.md:300:  `parseClaudeCliOutput` (the four-field Anthropic usage plus the served model).
docs/host-run-usage.md:302:A parse miss (no `turn.completed` event, no `result` usage) records an
docs/host-run-usage.md:303:`unavailable` final with a reason rather than inventing counts.
docs/host-run-usage.md:305:同样的诚实口径适用于 reviewer A/B：缺少 exact per-role historical envelope、
docs/host-run-usage.md:306:reviewer output、adjudication bytes 或 provider receipt 时结果是
docs/host-run-usage.md:307:`INCONCLUSIVE`，不是“0 token”或已证明的节省。B-235e 的独立 replay campaign
docs/host-run-usage.md:310:The one-line usage summary reflects the **actual append outcome**, not merely
docs/host-run-usage.md:311:that the provider envelope parsed. When the ledger append itself fails (a corrupt
docs/host-run-usage.md:312:ledger, or a lock-wait timeout that skips the write), the summary reports a
docs/host-run-usage.md:313:skipped state (`recorded: none`, reason `ledger_append_failed(...)`) and the
docs/host-run-usage.md:314:stderr line reads `usage: ledger_append_failed(...)` — it never claims
docs/host-run-usage.md:315:`usage recorded` for a row that never landed. This applies to both managed hosts;
docs/host-run-usage.md:316:the provider is still surfaced for attribution, but token counts stay null. A
docs/host-run-usage.md:317:provider record that BUILT fine but whose append failed is reported as an
docs/host-run-usage.md:318:append failure keyed on the parsed usage — it is **never degraded to
docs/host-run-usage.md:319:`source=unavailable`** (which would falsely read as "the provider reported
docs/host-run-usage.md:320:nothing"), and no second `unavailable` final is attempted for it.
docs/host-run-usage.md:322:The same honesty gate covers the **blocked rows**: a cap refusal claims
docs/host-run-usage.md:323:`recorded: blocked` (and, for a concurrency refusal, surfaces the blocked row's
docs/host-run-usage.md:324:`recordId`) only when the blocked row **actually appended**. When that append is
docs/host-run-usage.md:325:swallowed too, the refusal itself is unchanged — still fail-closed, no spawn,
docs/host-run-usage.md:326:non-zero exit — but the summary reports `recorded: none` with `recordId: null`
docs/host-run-usage.md:327:and a composed reason that keeps the refusal visible, e.g.
docs/host-run-usage.md:328:`hard_budget_exceeded (...); ledger_append_failed(...)` or
docs/host-run-usage.md:329:`concurrency_cap_exceeded (...); ledger_append_failed(...)`. A recordId is never
docs/host-run-usage.md:330:minted for a blocked row that never persisted.
docs/host-run-usage.md:332:## Provider execution surfaces
docs/host-run-usage.md:334:Every production provider spawn site carries a `ProviderExecutionSurfaceStatus`
docs/host-run-usage.md:335:and is enumerated by `provider-execution-inventory-contract`, which fails if a
docs/host-run-usage.md:336:new spawn path appears unclassified:
docs/host-run-usage.md:338:- `managed` — runs through ManagedHostRun (durable run identity, supervised
docs/host-run-usage.md:339:  process group, absolute deadline, one terminal receipt).
docs/host-run-usage.md:340:- `admission_only` — not managed-executed, but still routed through the shared
docs/host-run-usage.md:341:  admission boundary, so the concurrency cap below applies.
docs/host-run-usage.md:342:- `adapter_only` — a low-level adapter whose caller owns admission.
docs/host-run-usage.md:343:- `readiness_probe` — version/readiness checks only; never review evidence.
docs/host-run-usage.md:344:- `legacy_unmanaged` — neither managed nor admission-routed. Reserved and
docs/host-run-usage.md:345:  **currently empty by contract**: the inventory test asserts no surface uses
docs/host-run-usage.md:346:  it, so introducing one is a deliberate, reviewable act.
docs/host-run-usage.md:348:There is no `admission_managed` status — admission and managed execution are
docs/host-run-usage.md:349:independent properties, spelled `admission_only` and `managed`.
docs/host-run-usage.md:351:See `docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md` for
docs/host-run-usage.md:352:the decision record.
docs/host-run-usage.md:354:## Caps (fail-closed, before spawn)
docs/host-run-usage.md:356:With the usage ledger enabled, both caps run at the choke point BEFORE a host
docs/host-run-usage.md:357:is spawned, and each refusal attempts to record a
docs/host-run-usage.md:358:`decision.kind=blocked` ledger row (diagnostics-honest; an append failure is
docs/host-run-usage.md:359:reported as `recorded: none`). With `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=0`, budget enforcement
docs/host-run-usage.md:360:and every ledger row are disabled; the provider-process capacity admission
docs/host-run-usage.md:361:still runs before every spawn and refuses fail-closed without claiming a
docs/host-run-usage.md:362:blocked row was persisted.
docs/host-run-usage.md:364:- **Per-dispatch hard budget** — reuses the existing `LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS`
docs/host-run-usage.md:365:  preflight guard per call. An over-budget preflight estimate refuses with
docs/host-run-usage.md:366:  `reasonCode hard_budget_exceeded` before spawning.
docs/host-run-usage.md:367:- **Provider-process concurrency** — a shared slot registry under
docs/host-run-usage.md:368:  `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/`
docs/host-run-usage.md:369:  holds **fixed numbered slots** `slot-0.json` .. `slot-(cap-1).json`, one per
docs/host-run-usage.md:370:  live run (pid + `startedAt` + an acquire-minted **ownership token**).
docs/host-run-usage.md:371:  Admission and reclaim are serialized by the ownership-checked provider
docs/host-run-usage.md:372:  registry lock, then the selected fixed slot is created with exclusive `wx`.
docs/host-run-usage.md:373:  The lock makes the live-count check, stale reclaim, cap-lowering check and
docs/host-run-usage.md:374:  create one cross-process transaction, so simultaneous starts and corrupt-slot
docs/host-run-usage.md:375:  replacement cannot slip past the cap. When every index
docs/host-run-usage.md:376:  under `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_MAX_CONCURRENT` (default **4**; unset / invalid /
docs/host-run-usage.md:377:  `<=0` falls back to the default; an explicit larger value is honored) is
docs/host-run-usage.md:378:  held, the run refuses fail-closed with a non-zero exit, prints the live-run
docs/host-run-usage.md:379:  list, and, when the ledger is enabled, writes a blocked row with `reasonCode
docs/host-run-usage.md:380:  concurrency_cap_exceeded`.
docs/host-run-usage.md:381:  Slot reclaim is **ownership-aware** (mirroring the ledger-lock doctrine
docs/host-run-usage.md:382:  below): a slot with a recorded **dead pid** is reclaimed at any age; a slot
docs/host-run-usage.md:383:  whose metadata is **missing/corrupt** (the holder crashed between creating
docs/host-run-usage.md:384:  the file and its metadata landing) is reclaimed once its mtime exceeds the
docs/host-run-usage.md:385:  `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_SLOT_STALE_MS` orphan backstop (default **6h**); a slot
docs/host-run-usage.md:386:  with a **live** recorded pid is **never reclaimed by age** — a long host run
docs/host-run-usage.md:387:  keeps its admission and waiters refuse at cap. Reclaim re-verifies the
docs/host-run-usage.md:388:  occupant immediately before the unlink under the same registry lock and then
docs/host-run-usage.md:389:  re-creates exclusively, so a crashed run never wedges the cap and a racing
docs/host-run-usage.md:390:  reclaimer cannot delete a slot a new holder just re-acquired. Slot release on
docs/host-run-usage.md:391:  exit is best-effort, registry-serialized and **token-guarded**:
docs/host-run-usage.md:392:  the file is unlinked only while it still carries the releasing run's own
docs/host-run-usage.md:393:  token, so a reclaimed-and-re-acquired slot survives the original holder's
docs/host-run-usage.md:394:  late release. Raising the cap mid-flight exposes more indexes; lowering it
docs/host-run-usage.md:395:  counts every live high-index slot and refuses new starts until the total live

docs/host-run-usage.md:398:Blocked rows are provider-honest: a refusal records the provider of the managed
docs/host-run-usage.md:399:host that was asked to run (`openai` for codex or `anthropic` for claude), never
docs/host-run-usage.md:400:a hard-coded default.
docs/host-run-usage.md:402:The autopilot Claude repair launch (`lattice autopilot execute
docs/host-run-usage.md:403:--allowClaudeRepair`) passes the **same pre-spawn admission** in both ledger
docs/host-run-usage.md:404:modes. With the ledger ON, budget and capacity refusals can also write the
docs/host-run-usage.md:405:diagnostic blocked row. With the ledger OFF there are no usage rows or budget
docs/host-run-usage.md:406:guard, but capacity admission remains mandatory and the slot is still released
docs/host-run-usage.md:407:after the run.
docs/host-run-usage.md:409:The `cross_host_review` Codex leaf runs through ManagedHostRun and the same
docs/host-run-usage.md:410:provider admission (provider `openai`). It supports detach/resume by exact
docs/host-run-usage.md:411:`managedRunId`, never spawns a replacement on resume, and binds the terminal
docs/host-run-usage.md:412:`receiptId` into host-B verdict provenance. Budget/cap/provider failures still
docs/host-run-usage.md:413:produce an honest blocked/error decision; raw stdout is never gate evidence.
docs/host-run-usage.md:415:Concurrent runs' ledger appends are serialized by a cross-process lock at the
docs/host-run-usage.md:416:writer choke point (an atomic `llm-usage.jsonl.lock/` directory with a bounded
docs/host-run-usage.md:417:wait), so parallel host runs can never interleave appends and break the ledger
docs/host-run-usage.md:418:hash chain — a writer that cannot acquire the lock in time skips its append
docs/host-run-usage.md:419:(an honest under-count) rather than corrupting the chain. Lock reclaim is
docs/host-run-usage.md:420:ownership-aware: the acquirer records `owner.json` (holder pid + a unique
docs/host-run-usage.md:421:release token) inside the lock dir, and a held lock is reclaimed only when
docs/host-run-usage.md:422:that pid is dead, or — for an ownerless/corrupt lock, i.e. the holder crashed
docs/host-run-usage.md:423:between creating the dir and recording ownership — when the dir mtime exceeds
docs/host-run-usage.md:424:the `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER_LOCK_STALE_MS` orphan backstop. A live holder is
docs/host-run-usage.md:425:never reclaimed no matter how long it holds the lock (slow filesystem, GC
docs/host-run-usage.md:426:pause, suspension); release removes the lock only while `owner.json` still
docs/host-run-usage.md:427:carries the releaser's own token.
docs/host-run-usage.md:429:There is **no queuing** in this story: over the cap means refuse, not wait.
docs/host-run-usage.md:431:Set `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=0` to disable usage preflight/budget/final rows. It
docs/host-run-usage.md:432:does **not** disable ManagedHostRun ownership or provider-process admission.
