docs/host-run-usage.md:470:## `usage_sweep` (read-only retro-attribution)
docs/host-run-usage.md:473:lattice usage_sweep --since 2026-07-01 [--json]
docs/host-run-usage.md:476:`usage_sweep` stream-reads `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` and
docs/host-run-usage.md:477:`~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` since a cutoff and reports per-session token
docs/host-run-usage.md:478:totals, originator (desktop vs exec vs claude-code), cwd, first/last timestamps,
docs/host-run-usage.md:479:and `B-xxxx` story mentions, plus a per-story rollup and grand totals. It exists
docs/host-run-usage.md:480:to make runs that never went through `host_run` (interactive desktop sessions in
docs/host-run-usage.md:481:particular) at least visible.
docs/host-run-usage.md:483:- The report header states **NON-AUTHORITATIVE ESTIMATE** prominently in both
docs/host-run-usage.md:484:  the human table and `--json`. The totals come from host transcript stores, not
docs/host-run-usage.md:486:- It performs **no ledger backfill**: swept sessions are never written into the
docs/host-run-usage.md:488:- It is strictly **read-only**. The only write it can perform is an explicit
docs/host-run-usage.md:489:  `--out <path>` JSON report, and that write is create-only and fenced:
docs/host-run-usage.md:490:  - `--out` must be a **relative** path that resolves inside the project root;
docs/host-run-usage.md:491:    absolute paths and any `..` traversal escaping the root are refused
docs/host-run-usage.md:493:  - It only ever **creates a new report file** — the file is opened with the
docs/host-run-usage.md:494:    exclusive-create `wx` flag, so an already-existing target is refused
docs/host-run-usage.md:495:    atomically and `usage_sweep` can never overwrite or truncate anything
docs/host-run-usage.md:496:    (not even via a symlink at the target path).
docs/host-run-usage.md:497:  - It refuses to write through **symlinked ancestor directories**, and the
docs/host-run-usage.md:498:    resolved real path must still fall inside the (realpath'd) project root,
docs/host-run-usage.md:499:    so an inside-root symlink cannot redirect the report outside the project.
docs/host-run-usage.md:500:  - Missing report directories are created only **after** all of those checks
docs/host-run-usage.md:501:    pass.
docs/host-run-usage.md:502:  - Because `--out` writes a file into the material tree, a **non-empty `--out`
docs/host-run-usage.md:503:    is dynamically classified `storyScopedMutating`** by the ownership gate
docs/host-run-usage.md:504:    (F-014), so it is refused in read-only reviewer mode
docs/host-run-usage.md:505:    (`LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1`) and on a retired root; without `--out`,
docs/host-run-usage.md:506:    `usage_sweep` stays read-only and runnable by any session.
docs/host-run-usage.md:507:  - The **same `--out` boundary governs the CLI activity / hook layer** (F-028):
docs/host-run-usage.md:508:    a plain (no-`--out`) `usage_sweep` is read-only there too, so it runs **no
docs/host-run-usage.md:509:    pre/post command hooks** and writes **no activity-log entry by default** (the
docs/host-run-usage.md:510:    `LATTICE_ACTIVITY_RECORD_READONLY=1` read-only heartbeat override documented
docs/host-run-usage.md:511:    in docs/CLI.md still applies); a non-empty `--out` is treated as a write and
docs/host-run-usage.md:512:    runs the hooks + records activity like any other mutating command.
docs/host-run-usage.md:513:  - The same boundary also governs the **codex process-event surface** (F-032):
docs/host-run-usage.md:514:    under `LATTICE_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex` cli-engine appends a `codex_cli` event
docs/host-run-usage.md:515:    to the active story's `process-events.jsonl` after a command. That append is
docs/host-run-usage.md:516:    STORY metadata, so it obeys the identical read-only contract — a plain
docs/host-run-usage.md:517:    (no-`--out`) `usage_sweep` appends **no process event** (even with an
docs/host-run-usage.md:518:    inferred active story), while a non-empty `--out` (a write) records the
docs/host-run-usage.md:519:    process event like any other mutating command. The owner-lease heartbeat is
docs/host-run-usage.md:520:    intentionally exempt: it is keyed on the ownership class (only a
docs/host-run-usage.md:521:    `storyScopedMutating`/`dangerousMutating` write touches the lease), never on
docs/host-run-usage.md:522:    this read-only classification, so read-only session upkeep is unaffected.
docs/host-run-usage.md:526:- Usage rows **never gate the workflow** — they are `gateEvidence=false`
docs/host-run-usage.md:527:  diagnostics and are not consumed by any REVIEW/TEST/DONE/Authority gate.
docs/host-run-usage.md:528:- Interactive desktop host sessions are **out of reach** of the choke point;
docs/host-run-usage.md:529:  they are report-only via `usage_sweep`, never through `host_run`.
docs/host-run-usage.md:530:- `usage_sweep` never mutates story, ledger, or lifecycle state and never
docs/host-run-usage.md:531:  backfills the ledger.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:1:# Verification Context Pack
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:3:## Background
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:5:On 2026-05-20, the Python authority server introduced a stricter authority evidence gate: an L2 verifier may not submit a natural-language conclusion alone, but should submit structured evidence that is traceable, replayable, and coverable. The Proofbound CLI needs to synchronize with this protocol; otherwise a verifier may still miss key diffs, use weak test commands, or hand the server a conclusion that has no covering artifact.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:7:This document is the long-term source of truth on the Orchestrate side, describing how the Proofbound CLI and the Python authority server coordinate on the Verification Context Pack.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:11:The Proofbound CLI is responsible for mechanically generating the Verification Context Pack. The external Python authority server is responsible for issuing verifier jobs, validating the evidence envelope, and enforcing gate adequacy. The fields, digest rules, and default coverage semantics on both sides should stay consistent; however, the Python-side preset, limit, and gate details may be regarded as locally-landed facts in Orchestrate only when there is an explicit code/doc re

ference in this repo.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:13:The Context Pack is the verifier's default reading boundary, not a natural-language suggestion. It should contain changed files, changed hunks, changed symbols, source snippets, checklist item ids, test intent refs, oracle refs, required commands, risk tags, limitations, token budget, the truncated marker, and the parent digest of an expansion pack.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:14:When the diff contains deleted files, the default source snippets should still provide readable deletion context; if the source is no longer in the worktree, the CLI must derive the snippet content from the diff/removed lines rather than leaving it blank.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:16:A verifier may request an expanded context, but the expansion must carry an `expansionReason`. If the external authority server has its own `maxContextPackExpansionDepth`, `maxContextPackEstimatedTokens`, or preset-level limits, those are authority-side expected/to-be-aligned constraints and should not be written as locally-landed facts in this repo's documentation. An expansion is not a way to bypass the context pack, but forms a parent-linked pack chain.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:18:## CLI Responsibilities
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:20:- `verification_context_pack_create` mechanically generates a pack from the current git diff, and does not write story metadata.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:21:- `verification_context_pack_expand` generates a controlled expansion based on a parent pack, and must state the reason for the expansion.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:22:- `digestVerificationContextPack` maintains canonical digest parity with Python's `VerificationContextPack.digest()`.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:23:- `buildTargetBoundEvidenceEnvelope` and `EvidenceCollector` by default include the context pack's required refs in `coveredRefs`, and populate `verificationContextPackId`, `verificationContextPackDigest`, and `inspectedPackRefs`.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:24:- In the CLI command policy, these two commands should be read-only / all phases / non-destructive.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:26:## Server Coordination
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:28:The external Python authority server's verifier job is expected to bind a signed context pack and digest. When L2 evidence is submitted, the authority side typically checks whether the pack id, digest, producerRunId, and diffHash in the evidence match the server-issued verifier job; this repo is only responsible for the CLI-side fields and digest output.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:30:The external authority gate is expected to require that the pack's files, hunks, oracle refs, test intent refs, required commands, and so on are covered, otherwise the evidence is insufficient. The responsibility currently landed in this repo is to stably map these required refs onto evidence surfaces such as `coveredRefs` / `inspectedPackRefs` for the authority side to consume.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:32:If the authority side in the future, or an external deployment, enables presets such as `anti-hallucination` or `strict-ci`, the verifier job is expected to be required to carry a context pack; as of this repo's current state, these preset names are external authority constraints, not established facts of this repo's local gate.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:34:## Verification Commands
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:36:On the CLI side, at minimum run:
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:39:npm --prefix packages/main run build
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:40:npm --prefix packages/main run test:verification-context-pack
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:41:npm --prefix packages/main run test:command-ownership-contract
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:44:On the external Python authority server side, to verify protocol alignment, run the corresponding regression:
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:47:uv run pytest -q
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:52:When modifying the authority/evidence/context-pack-related code of the Proofbound CLI in the future, you must first establish or restore a Story per Orchestrate's Proofbound story flow, and run `lattice session_brief` and `lattice aux_doc_list`. Unless the user explicitly requests a quick patch, do not bypass Story/checklist/verificationEvidence.
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:54:Whenever you modify any of the following, you must synchronously check the protocol fields and tests of the external Python authority server:
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:56:- `packages/main/src/core/authority-contracts.ts`
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:57:- `packages/main/src/core/evidence-collector.ts`
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:58:- `packages/main/src/core/verification-context-pack.ts`

docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:60:- `packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts`
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:61:- `packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts`
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:63:Key checks on the corresponding external Python side:
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:65:- `cord_team.schemas.verification.VerificationContextPack`
docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:66:- `cord_team.schemas.command.EvidenceEnvelope`

docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:1:# Unlock Layer 2 Engineering Baseline Suite
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:5:> Status: execution plan for formal unlock

docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:7:> Non-goal: this document does not unlock Layer 2 by itself and does not unlock Loop Engineering, Production Safety, or global Capability Claim
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:11:This document defines the execution plan to formally unlock Layer 2 Engineering
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:12:Baseline capability.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:14:The goal is not to add another framework layer or create a stronger-looking
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:15:claim. The goal is to prove, through an evidence-backed Engineering baseline
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:16:suite, that Proofbound can handle realistic engineering work under scoped,
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:17:reviewed, gated, and auditable conditions.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:19:The core question answered by this unlock is:
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:21:```text
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:22:Can Proofbound complete realistic engineering tasks with correct scope control,
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:23:regression protection, review evidence, and fail-closed proof gates?
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:26:The allowed claim after unlock is:
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:28:```text
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:29:Proofbound has passed the Layer 2 Engineering Baseline and can claim real
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:30:engineering development baseline capability under gated, evidence-backed
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:34:The unlock does not allow these claims:
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:36:- Proofbound can run unattended development.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:37:- Proofbound is production-grade.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:38:- Proofbound can autonomously develop arbitrary projects.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:39:- Proofbound can skip Loop Engineering.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:40:- Proofbound can skip Production Safety.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:41:- Proofbound can treat local CLI status as production Authority.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:42:- Proofbound can turn host transcripts into capability proof by relabeling them.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:46:All execution must follow these four principles:
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:48:```text
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:49:Do not optimize for the sake of optimization.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:51:Only fix real correctness issues.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:52:Preserve consistency of logic.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:55:Operational meaning:
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:57:- Do not add new abstractions just to make the unlock look more advanced.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:58:- Do not change baseline definitions during execution unless a real correctness
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:59:  issue is found.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:60:- Do not downgrade a failed baseline into PASS for momentum.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:61:- Do not let local diagnostic artifacts become formal proof.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:62:- Do not expand the claim beyond the evidence.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:63:- Do not unlock higher layers from Layer 2 evidence.
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:65:## 3. Current State
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:67:Layer 2 now has the proof path required to consume formal evidence, but the

docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer2-ENG-suite.md:110:## 5. Required Engineering Baselines

docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:5:Source finding: docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-ledger-status-review-findings.md — B-b550 M7 completeness-critic divergences (a) stale-evidence disagreement and (b) closeout second-gate
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:6:Date: 2026-07-05
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:10:B-b550's completeness critic found two places where the milestone observability
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:11:surface and the *designed* DONE gate (`evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence`,
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:12:`packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts`, consumed by the DONE transition at
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:13:`packages/main/src/handlers/phase-gates.ts`) gave **contradictory verdicts on the
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:16:- **(a) STALE-EVIDENCE DISAGREEMENT.** `milestone_status` demotes a milestone row
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:17:  to `groups.current` with `statusDetail=…; evidence=stale` when its verification
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:18:  evidence hash no longer matches the current binding (via `evidenceIsCovering` →
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:19:  `evidenceFreshnessRisks`, `packages/main/src/core/milestone-status.ts`). But
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:20:  `evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence` resolved milestone coverage through
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:21:  `evidenceCoversIntent`, which checked only `result === 'pass'` (or a permanent
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:22:  non-failing waiver) and was **completely freshness-blind**. So the same stale
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:23:  ledger that `milestone_status` demoted could still PASS the DONE gate — two
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:24:  surfaces, opposite verdicts on identical evidence.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:26:- **(b) CLOSEOUT SECOND-GATE.** `captureMilestoneCloseoutSnapshotFromStore`
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:27:  (`packages/main/src/handlers/milestone-status.ts`) is invoked from
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:28:  `packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts` inside
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:29:  `if (args.phase === 'DONE')` — **after** `actor.send` has already moved the story
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:31:  rows or any risk. Because a stale/incomplete ledger throws, closeout acted as an
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:32:  **undesigned second DONE gate with throw-semantics** that diverged from
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:33:  `evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence`: it could abort a DONE the designed gate had
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:34:  already permitted, and it did so *after* the state transition was committed.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:38:Strictness lives in the single designed gate; default behavior must NOT newly block.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:40:### (a) Make the DONE gate honor milestone evidence freshness — as a gated, non-blocking diagnostic
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:42:- `evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence` now detects milestones whose base coverage
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:43:  passes but whose **only** covering evidence is stale, and emits a new
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:44:  `stale_milestone_evidence` diagnostic gap (severity `warn`, in
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:45:  `packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts`). Because the report's `blocking`
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:46:  is `mode === 'enforce' && gaps.length > 0`, this gap — exactly like every other
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:47:  milestone gap — is a **NON-BLOCKING diagnostic under the default `observe` mode
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:48:  and only blocks under `enforce`**. No new hard block was added to observe mode.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:49:- Agreement is **by construction**: both surfaces call the same exported predicate
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:50:  `evidenceIsStaleCovering` (`packages/main/src/core/milestone-status.ts`).
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:51:  `milestone_status` keeps its full-risk demotion; the DONE gate calls the
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:52:  predicate with `mismatchOnly = true`.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:53:- **Staleness = mismatch, not absence.** The gate flags a milestone only when a
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:54:  *bound* hash genuinely disagrees with the current binding (a `stale <hash> …`
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:55:  risk), never when evidence simply *lacks* a binding (a `missing … binding`
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:56:  risk). This matches the finding's wording ("evidence hash no longer matches")
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:57:  and is the conservative choice: evidence recorded before binding capture is
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:58:  unbound, not stale, so it is not newly blocked.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:59:- The current binding is plumbed via a new optional
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:60:  `ProofStoryDiagnosticInput.currentEvidenceBinding` computed with the *same*
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:61:  `currentMilestoneStatusEvidenceBinding` + `resolveGitCwd` that `milestone_status`
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:62:  uses (`packages/main/src/handlers/proofstory.ts`,
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:63:  `packages/main/src/handlers/phase-gates.ts`). When absent, freshness is not
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:64:  evaluated and base coverage semantics are preserved — the change is opt-in and
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:65:  backward-compatible.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:67:### (b) Make closeout a pure snapshot capture, not a second gate
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:69:- `captureMilestoneCloseoutSnapshotFromStore` no longer propagates the strict
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:70:  builder throw. It now **degrades to a non-throwing `{ status: 'skipped', reason:
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:71:  'closeout_snapshot_unbuildable' }`** when `buildMilestoneCloseoutSnapshot` cannot
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:72:  build a snapshot (`packages/main/src/handlers/milestone-status.ts`):
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:73:  capture what exists, and when the report is incomplete/risky/stale simply record
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:74:  that no auditable snapshot was written. The single designed gate
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:75:  (`evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence`, which already ran *before* the DONE transition)
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:76:  remains the sole authority on whether DONE is allowed.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:78:  (`packages/main/src/core/milestone-status.ts`) is unchanged: it still
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:79:  rejects an incomplete/risky report, so CHK-005's "a stale-only status report is
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:80:  rejected by buildMilestoneCloseoutSnapshot" negative control still holds. Only
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:81:  the DONE-time capture *wrapper* is made non-blocking.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:83:## Why this does not weaken the contract or block existing DONE flows
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:85:- **Read-only / PLAN-only milestone contract is untouched.** `milestone_status` /
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:86:  `milestone_closeout` remain read-only observers; their args-boundary asserts and
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:87:  read shape are unchanged. The reconciliation touches only (a) the DONE gate's
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:88:  coverage predicate and (b) the DONE-time capture wrapper.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:89:- **Default (`observe`) behavior does not newly block.** The new gap is severity
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:90:  `warn`; under `observe`, `blocking` stays `false`. A DONE that passed before this
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:91:  change with the same inputs still passes under `observe`.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md:92:- **Currently-passing DONE flows are preserved.** B-b550's confirmed-ledger

docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:95:## Implementation Guards
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:97:- JSON-mode progress must use stderr or a structured parent-consumed side channel; stdout remains reserved for the JSON result.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:98:- Progress and heartbeat writes must flush immediately.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:99:- Validation lock ownership must not rely on PID alone. Use `pid + processStartTime`, a per-run UUID, or an OS-level lock handle so PID reuse does not make stale locks look active.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:100:- Lock liveness checks must be host-neutral. POSIX-only `/proc` checks are insufficient unless wrapped behind a platform abstraction.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:101:- Forced exit should use a two-stage shutdown: request graceful termination, allow a short cleanup grace period, then hard-kill only if the child remains alive.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:102:- Evidence written after forced exit must identify runner infrastructure failure separately from test failure.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:106:- `lattice validate --story=<id> --json` emits progress for configured commands.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:107:- `--json` stdout remains valid JSON; heartbeat/progress events do not pollute the machine-readable result.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:108:- Heartbeat/progress events are flushed immediately and are visible to the parent process before the idle deadline.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:109:- Long-running validate commands emit heartbeat at a bounded interval, preferably 30 seconds.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:110:- `story_advance --phase=TEST` is not killed while validate is actively heartbeating.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:111:- A command that exceeds its own `timeoutMs` still fails.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:112:- Failure output identifies the exact validate command that failed or timed out.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:113:- Forced exit does not leave a fresh-looking validation lock for a vanished process.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:114:- Stale lock detection is resilient to PID reuse and works through a host-neutral abstraction.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:115:- Watchdog termination allows child cleanup before hard kill.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:116:- Infra failure is not recorded as ordinary test failure.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:117:- Existing gate strictness is preserved.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:121:- Do not remove the idle watchdog.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:122:- Do not make validate pass when tests fail.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:123:- Do not skip `lattice validate`.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:124:- Do not reduce configured validate commands.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:125:- Do not use unlimited timeout.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:126:- Do not rely on POSIX-only process checks without a host-neutral wrapper.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:127:- Do not change unrelated story behavior.

docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:144:- A later closeout idle/max timeout preserves any already-observed validation disposition, evidence basis, and refusal reasons; only the later terminal result/layer changes to `timed_out` and `idle|max`. The command-level `done_prepare` budget is the exact sum of routine validation plus each enabled closeout phase once (five non-validation phases, plus DONE-required only when enabled). CLI named deadline errors propagate through routine verifier execution so a command deadline that lands between watchdog polling ticks retains `timeoutLayer=max`.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:146:- Closeout segments check the parent watchdog before and after each segment and await cooperative abort cleanup. Synchronous JavaScript is inherently non-preemptible, so it stops at the first deadline/checkpoint boundary. Pure in-process closeout segments spawn no descendants, making process-tree ESRCH evidence not applicable there; descendant cleanup is required and tested only for validation/phase paths that actually spawn children.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:148:DONE-required execution and reuse use one bounded contract:
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:150:- The DONE-required phase budget is the safe sum of effective sequential command timeouts plus bounded grace. A phase-specific override wins the global phase override, which wins the derived budget. The direct `done_required_validate` CLI max covers that derived phase; the `done_prepare` CLI max covers routine validation plus every enabled closeout phase. An explicit `LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` remains authoritative. Each effective command timeout is capped at Node's maximum legal timer delay before arming the real timer, so a huge configured value cannot overflow into an immediate timeout. Structured `failed` / `timed_out` / `blocked` results remain parseable on stdout and exit nonzero; routine `done_prepare` idle/max aborts use the same terminal timeout shape and release child processes, timers, and locks for an immediate rerun.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:151:- `done_prepare` defaults `reuseFreshDoneRequired=true`, independently of post-closeout `reuseFreshValidation`. Reuse requires the canonical DONE-required evaluator to pass and evidence HEAD to equal current HEAD, or be its ancestor with every path touched by every intervening commit classified as trusted story metadata (including modify-then-revert history). HEAD must remain unchanged across evaluation. Any code, config, non-metadata, non-ancestor, unreadable evidence/lineage, or concurrent HEAD movement refuses reuse.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:152:- `validate:false` means `disposition=skipped_explicitly` and `result=not_run`; it neither executes nor reuses nor manufactures evidence, while reporting `existingEvidenceBasis=fresh|stale|missing`. Executed and reused paths report `disposition`, `result`, `refusalReasons`, and any `timeoutLayer` in human and JSON output.
docs/requirements/decisions/validate-progress-heartbeat-forced-exit-cleanup-execution-plan.md:153:- Progress and heartbeat output uses stderr/the logging side channel, never JSON stdout. Reporter failures are diagnostic-only. Heartbeats refresh idle liveness only; command, phase, idle, and absolute max deadlines, child-tree termination, lock release, and timer cleanup remain independent.

docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:12:## 0. Why We Cannot Copy the Reference Picture Directly
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:14:The reference picture (Claude Code Agent Monitor) is essentially a **transcript inversion**: it reads the hook events of `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` and reverse-engineers the token / tool / session of a single host (Claude Code) runtime into a board. Its "Completed / Error" is **host runtime state**, not delivery authority.
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:16:The core of the next-generation Proofbound is **Host-Neutral**: it fully decouples "complete" from the host runtime. Any host (Codex, Claude Code, a future headless runner) is just an **adapter**, which can only execute the authorized task package and submit an **auditable receipt**. The authority layer recognizes only Canonical Story + receipt-backed evidence, and the host-local "it's green" is always only `local-evidence`.

docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:65:### 2.0 CLI JSON stdout contract (B-7fc2)
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:67:The adapter / dashboard / smoke can treat the following assumptions as a hard contract:
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:69:- **stdout in machine JSON mode is JSON.parse-able as a single document.** When the caller passes `--json` or `--format=json`, the corresponding command's stdout must be "**a single JSON document + an optional trailing newline**," with no next-step hint, decorative text, ANSI control characters, or a second JSON document concatenated after it. The caller **does not need** to do substring extraction (`extractFirstJsonObject` / regex matching `\{...\}`, etc.); a direct `JSON.parse(stdout)` must succeed.
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:70:- **Human-readable guidance goes only through text mode or stderr.** The `→ Validation passed`, `→ Next step…`, and other next-step hints of commands such as `lattice validate` are appended only in **non-JSON mode**. `stderr` is used for logs / progress / config notices and does not pollute the stdout contract.
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:71:- **Implementation-choice note**: the contract is enforced by the unified choke point of the CLI output pipeline (`cli-engine.ts`) — a hit on `wantsMachineJson(args)` skips `decorateResult`, and all hint-registered commands (including `validate`) automatically comply. If a `--json` / `--format=json` command is added later, a hit on the same detector automatically gains contract protection, with no need to patch each one separately.
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:72:- **Regression protection**: `tests/cli-json-stdout-contract-smoke.ts` (`packages/main/src/tasks/cli-json-stdout-contract-smoke.ts`) spawns a real CLI subprocess and directly `JSON.parse(stdout)` — any regression that concatenates a hint back into JSON mode will immediately turn the smoke red. Text mode is checked at the same time to ensure it keeps `→ Validation passed`, preventing "deleting the human hint along with the fix to JSON mode."
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:74:> Actual effect: the dashboard / host adapter treats the Proofbound CLI's `--format=json` / `--json` stdout as a stable contract, with no need to handle the past anti-pattern where `validate --json` concatenated `→ Validation passed. Next: …` at the end, causing `JSON.parse` to fail.
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:76:### 2.1 Three schema/authority Pitfalls the Adapter Must Solve First
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:78:0. **The resolver JSON surface is currently missing (the real first task of M1)**: in practice, `lattice status --format=json` / `--json` and `session_brief` **both ignore the flag and only return Markdown**, and `--help` has no `--format` parameter either. So M1 is **not "writing an adapter to consume ready-made JSON"**, but first **adding/extending a machine-readable resolver surface** that returns `{storyId, authority, mirrorPhase, authoritativePhase, authoritativeCwd, worktreePath}` for each active story. Before it lands, having the UI adapter parse Markdown is a fragile anti-pattern and is forbidden.
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:79:1. **worktree authority vs main mirror (the most critical)**: running `story_export B-xxx` at the repo root reads the **main mirror** (often stuck at INIT_CHECK, stale); only running it inside `.worktrees/B-xxx` gives the **authoritative** phase. The adapter **must first use the (0) resolver to get `authoritativeCwd`, then export in the correct cwd** — it cannot just aggregate the root's export.
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:80:2. **The parallel projection does not share the same envelope**: `parallel_wave_create` has the full `storyRefs/hostCandidates/mergeOrder`; but `parallel_status` / `parallel_merge_queue` / `parallel_report` **do not repeat the full envelope** (the source of truth `lattice-parallel-wave.md` §Projection JSON Contracts states this explicitly). The adapter must write a mapping per **each command's real schema**, and cannot assume all fields are present.

docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:186:## 5. The Essential Difference Between Host-Neutral and the Reference Picture (a thesis that can be stated in one sentence)
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:188:| Dimension | Reference picture (transcript monitor) | Proofbound Host-Neutral Dashboard |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:190:| Data source | `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` hook events | worktree + Story store + L0 CLI projection |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:191:| Definition of "complete" | the host runtime marks Completed | **receipt-backed `server-receipt` tier** |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:192:| host binding | hard-bound to Claude Code | adapter-ized (codex / claude-code / runner are equal) |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:193:| Failure expression | a red Error card | **Visible Degradation** (with fallback + recovery + authorityImpact) |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:194:| Recoverable | none | **Recovery Point** is a first-class citizen |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:195:| Tamper-proof | none | `canonicalStoryDigest` / `gateInputDigest` sha256 |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:196:| Authority | monitoring is the truth | **read-only projection, never authorizing** (`authority.productionDone=false` hardcoded) |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:200:## 6. Milestones (anchored to real story progress)
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:202:> Each milestone maps to a real CLI + the current story state, and introduces no new authority path.
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:204:| M | Name | Delivery (all L0 read-only) | Real story dependency | Exit criterion |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:206:| **M1** | Resolver surface + Read-only adapter | **First add a machine-readable resolver JSON surface** (returns `storyId/authority/mirrorPhase/authoritativePhase/authoritativeCwd/worktreePath` for active stories), then wrap the `story_export`/`parallel_*`/`host_*`/`authority_status` adapter, zero writes | `status`/`session_brief` currently only Markdown (needs extending); the other CLIs already exist | **The first acceptance item** = the resolver JSON surface exists and the UI does not need to parse Markdown; all 8 concept fields can be obtained from the CLI JSON |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:207:| **M2** | Authority Ladder + Story Board | The Overview three-tier ladder + the tier-columned board + degradation coloring | M1 resolver + `story_export` aggregation | `localEvidenceCount` lands correctly in the local-evidence column; the localDone↔productionDone GAP card is shown |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:208:| **M3** | Capability & Conduit | Capability Matrix + Host Registry + `conduit_explain` hover | B-aa98 (Host Overflow adapter) | claude-code's receipt-verify degradation is visible and comes with a recovery |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:209:| **M4** | Promote Thread + Trajectory to first-class schemas | Define the Thread / Trajectory projection schema on top of `story_export.lineage.processEvents`; Thread Inspector + Trajectory Timeline | B-5cdc (runner job claim / provider event flow, **already DONE and can serve as a base**) | A single-host task-package thread can be replayed; the lifecycle trajectory is connected |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:210:| **M5** | Recovery Console + productionDone true value wired through | recoveryPoints/guidance aggregation; when B-2522's receipt-backed verifier lands, the server-receipt column is non-empty for the first time | **B-2522 (receipt-backed verifier + local/enforce E2E); the README makes clear the enforce path is not yet end-to-end** | At least 1 story enters the `server-receipt` tier, and the change in the gap metric is visible |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:211:| **M6** | Wave scheduling view + Dispatch Console | Parallel lanes + merge queue + task-package dispatch (`spawned=false` / `requiresRunnerConfirmation=true`) | The full parallel-wave set (already exists) | The dispatch projection does not auto-spawn, does not auto-merge, and does not submit a receipt |
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:213:**Key order**: M1→M2 first establishes the thesis that "host-local green ≠ production done" (the data is already ready); M5 is the high point of the Host-Neutral closed loop — once B-2522 submits a verifiable receipt, the Dashboard's `server-receipt` column **lights up for the first time**, and the whole table goes from "the honest anxiety of all-local-evidence" to "a production done that is on record."
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:219:1. **The Dashboard is an L0 read-only projection**: it may write the export file requested by the caller, but **never** changes story metadata / process evidence / lifecycle / receipt / authority / and does not spawn a runner.
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:220:2. **Never claim production DONE**: all projections hard-carry `authority.productionDone=false`, `authorityChanged=false`, `receiptRefs=[]`, unless a **verified** receipt appears in the export.
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:221:3. **A local PASS is not upgraded**: a host-local "green" always stops at `local-evidence`, and rollout_check / wave / handoff cannot promote it to production authority.
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:222:4. **Degradation must be visible**: any capability gap enters `degradations[]` and is marked with `authorityImpact`, and is not silently swallowed.
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:223:5. **Tamper-proof**: display `canonicalStoryDigest`, alarm when the diff does not match, and do not trust a "Canonical Story that has been modified."
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:224:6. **Enforce is not yet closed-loop**: the README makes clear the `enforce` path is "Not implemented end-to-end yet"; even with a Python authority env configured, the `shadow`-mode `accepted:true` is only `thin-client-transport-accepted`, **not a verified receipt**. Before the B-2522 receipt flow is wired through, the `server-receipt` column must stay empty, and `productionDone`/`receiptVerified` must stay `false`. The Dashboard must not render shadow accepted as "complete."
docs/requirements/decisions/host-neutral-observability-console.md:226:> The source of truth is the Authority Boundary of `docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-parallel-wave.md`, `packages/main/src/core/canonical-story.ts`, and `README.md` (Authority modes off/shadow/enforce). This document is a read-only console design projection, and does not modify any authority semantics.

docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:53:All execution must follow these four principles:
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:55:```text

docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:59:Preserve consistency of logic.

docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:538:## 13. Formal Unlock Steps
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:540:The formal execution should use this sequence:
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:544:| 0 | Freeze target state | Main/workspace target and material hash are selected. |
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:545:| 1 | Refresh lower layers | Layer 1 and Layer 2 proof are fresh and unlocked for the target using the selected artifact roots, not an assumed default root. |
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:546:| 2 | Verify Layer 3 formal evaluator path | The evaluator can authorize `loop-engineering` while keeping Production Safety and global Capability Claim locked; otherwise status is `BLOCKED: missing Layer 3 formal evaluator`. |
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:547:| 3 | Create Layer 3 suite run id | `suiteRunId` is stable for all UDM baselines. |
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:548:| 4 | Materialize UDM run directories | All artifacts are under `.lattice/artifacts/baseline/layer3-loop-engineering-unlock`. |
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:549:| 5 | Execute 10 UDM baselines | Each baseline has required files and final report. |
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:550:| 6 | Run fail-closed traps | Open loop, stale evidence, missing review, missing validation, missing receipt, and false-DONE traps block. |
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:551:| 7 | Run two-host review | Claude CLI and Codex CLI independently PASS or report real blockers. |
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:552:| 8 | Generate Loop suite report | 10/10 covered, no missing baseline, no false DONE. |
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:553:| 9 | Run Layer 3 formal claim evaluator | `loopEngineeringClaim=UNLOCKED` only if all lower and Layer 3 proof is fresh. |
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:554:| 10 | Verify higher-layer locks | Production Safety and global Capability Claim remain `LOCKED`. |
docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:555:| 11 | Write delivery summary | State the exact allowed and forbidden claims. |

docs/requirements/decisions/done-full-test-gate-execution-plan.md:5:The verified gap is that the local DONE gate currently consumes evidence produced by `lattice validate`, and `lattice validate` runs the configured validation subset when `validate.commands` exists. docs/requirements/decisions/done-full-test-gate-execution-plan.md:7:Important caveat: this proves a gate coverage gap, not that current main `npm test` is red. The claim is about what the current gate is capable of proving. It does not assert a live root-suite failure on `main`.

docs/requirements/decisions/done-full-test-gate-execution-plan.md:396:- A later closeout idle/max timeout preserves any already-observed validation disposition, evidence basis, and refusal reasons; only the later terminal result/layer changes to `timed_out` and `idle|max`. The command-level `done_prepare` budget is the exact sum of routine validation plus each enabled closeout phase once (five non-validation phases, plus DONE-required only when enabled). CLI named deadline errors propagate through routine verifier execution so a command deadline that lands between watchdog polling ticks retains `timeoutLayer=max`.
docs/requirements/decisions/done-full-test-gate-execution-plan.md:398:- Closeout segments check the parent watchdog before and after each segment and await cooperative abort cleanup. Synchronous JavaScript is inherently non-preemptible, so it stops at the first deadline/checkpoint boundary. Pure in-process closeout segments spawn no descendants, making process-tree ESRCH evidence not applicable there; descendant cleanup is required and tested only for validation/phase paths that actually spawn children.
docs/requirements/decisions/done-full-test-gate-execution-plan.md:400:DONE-required execution and reuse use one bounded contract:
docs/requirements/decisions/done-full-test-gate-execution-plan.md:402:- The DONE-required phase budget is the safe sum of effective sequential command timeouts plus bounded grace. A phase-specific override wins the global phase override, which wins the derived budget. The direct `done_required_validate` CLI max covers that derived phase; the `done_prepare` CLI max covers routine validation plus every enabled closeout phase. An explicit `LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` remains authoritative. Each effective command timeout is capped at Node's maximum legal timer delay before arming the real timer, so a huge configured value cannot overflow into an immediate timeout. Structured `failed` / `timed_out` / `blocked` results remain parseable on stdout and exit nonzero; routine `done_prepare` idle/max aborts use the same terminal timeout shape and release child processes, timers, and locks for an immediate rerun.
docs/requirements/decisions/done-full-test-gate-execution-plan.md:403:- `done_prepare` defaults `reuseFreshDoneRequired=true`, independently of post-closeout `reuseFreshValidation`. Reuse requires the canonical DONE-required evaluator to pass and evidence HEAD to equal current HEAD, or be its ancestor with every path touched by every intervening commit classified as trusted story metadata (including modify-then-revert history). HEAD must remain unchanged across evaluation. Any code, config, non-metadata, non-ancestor, unreadable evidence/lineage, or concurrent HEAD movement refuses reuse.
docs/requirements/decisions/done-full-test-gate-execution-plan.md:404:- `validate:false` means `disposition=skipped_explicitly` and `result=not_run`; it neither executes nor reuses nor manufactures evidence, while reporting `existingEvidenceBasis=fresh|stale|missing`. Executed and reused paths report `disposition`, `result`, `refusalReasons`, and any `timeoutLayer` in human and JSON output.
docs/requirements/decisions/done-full-test-gate-execution-plan.md:405:- Progress and heartbeat output uses stderr/the logging side channel, never JSON stdout. Reporter failures are diagnostic-only. Heartbeats refresh idle liveness only; command, phase, idle, and absolute max deadlines, child-tree termination, lock release, and timer cleanup remain independent.

docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:17:This plan defines how `Proof-or-Stop` can be extended to PINN research workflows as a **claim-admissibility control layer**.
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:19:It is not a scientific claim engine.
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:21:The optimization is to prevent unsupported or stale PINN claims from advancing across lifecycle stages.
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:23:> Proof-or-Stop for PINNs does not prove PDE correctness or improve solver accuracy by itself.  
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:24:> It proves whether a PINN claim is admissible enough (with bound evidence) to advance.
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:26:## Problem Statement
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:28:Research teams often upgrade the strength of a claim from narrative evidence to
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:29:stronger claims before evidence is complete (training loss vs residual, or single
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:30:checklist success vs actual reproducibility). Proof-or-Stop already has strong
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:31:local controls, but this gap is especially visible in scientific domains where
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:32:claims are high-value and easy to overstate.
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:34:This plan introduces a domain pack so PINN lifecycle transitions are mechanically
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:35:bound to reproducible evidence, and unsupported claims are forced to repair,
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:40:What we do:
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:42:- add a formal PINN domain pack to existing `Proof-or-Stop` core controls;
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:43:- define admissibility identity for PINN artifacts (spec/training/config/checkpoint/grid/verifier/evidence bindings);
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:44:- define lifecycle gate predicates and failure behavior (`advance`, `repair`, `degrade`, `stop`);
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:45:- add a bounded benchmark for admissibility control quality.
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:47:What we do not do:
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:49:- claim that this proves PDE solutions mathematically;
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:50:- improve PINN model quality, architecture, optimization, or scientific validity;
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:51:- remove existing Proof-or-Stop gates, evidence requirements, or claim-boundary
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:53:- add uncontrolled API changes outside the PINN domain extension.

docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:59:- if no robust command set can be defined for a phase, that phase remains blocked.

docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:311:This extension is meaningful even if not scientific verification:

docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:317:  them into research workflow governance.
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:321:Potential wording for future docs (non-abstract, non-results section):

docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:324:> control. It does not solve the PDE or prove numerical correctness. It proves

docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:326:> evidence to advance across lifecycle stages such as training, residual verification,
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-pinn-claim-admissibility-execution-plan.md:327:> boundary-condition checking, baseline comparison, reproducibility, and result reporting.

docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:1:# Decision: Milestone-triggered gate-mode default stays `observe`
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:3:Status: decided
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:4:Story: B-f7b3 (CHK-009)
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:5:Source finding: docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-ledger-status-review-findings.md — M3/M7 (gate-mode default question)
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:6:Date: 2026-07-05
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:10:The B-b550 audit (M3 correction) established that the ProofStory strict-DONE milestone
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:11:gate only *blocks* when `doneGateMode === 'enforce'`; the default is `observe`, under
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:12:which milestone gaps are surfaced as advisories but do not block DONE. M7 asked whether
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:13:milestone-*triggered* stories should default to `enforce` instead of `observe`.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:17:**`observe` stays the default. Do NOT flip `doneGateMode`'s default to `enforce`, and do
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:18:NOT build an implicit "enforce-for-triggered" default.** `enforce` remains strictly
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:19:opt-in per project via `.lattice` config (`proofStory.doneGateMode: "enforce"`).
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:21:This closes findings M3/M7 with a recorded decision rather than a code change to the
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:22:default. It does not weaken the read-only / PLAN-only milestone contract: the strict path
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:23:is left exactly as-is, reachable only by explicit operator opt-in.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:25:## Rationale
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:27:Source facts (verified in this worktree):
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:29:- `doneGateMode` resolves via `loadConfig(root).proofStory?.doneGateMode ?? 'observe'`
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:30:  (`packages/main/src/core/config.ts`; consumed at
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:31:  `packages/main/src/handlers/phase-gates.ts`, in `configuredProofStoryMode`). It is a single **flat,
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:32:  project-wide** default — there is no per-story or per-trigger mode selection anywhere in
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:33:  the code today. So the literal option "enforce-for-triggered" corresponds to no existing
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:34:  switch; delivering it would require BUILDING new machinery that keys the mode off
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:35:  `hasMilestonePath` / `classifyTriggers`. That is itself a wide behavior change and is out
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:36:  of scope for a decision item.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:37:- `hasMilestonePath` (`packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts`) auto-activates the
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:38:  strict path whenever a ledger has ≥1 milestone OR a slice plan exists OR the
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:39:  `milestone-ledger` trigger fired. That trigger (`classifyTriggers` in `proofstory.ts`)
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:40:  fires on **fuzzy regex text signals** (≥2 structural rows, "all/every/remaining
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:41:  milestones", "M1-M5" ranges, explicit milestone mentions). Defaulting *triggered* stories
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:42:  to `enforce` would therefore hand a hard DONE-blocking gate to any story whose prose
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:43:  happens to match those regexes — a wide, surprising blast radius across every
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:44:  milestone-triggered story, including in-flight ones.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:45:- The B-b550 audit confirmed the milestone surface is **safe today**. The goal of this
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:46:  program is to close observability/coverage gaps, not to introduce a behavior change that
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:47:  could block existing DONE flows (e.g. B-b550's own confirmed-ledger closeout).
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:49:Conclusion: making `enforce` the default is a high-blast-radius behavior change that the
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:50:audit does not require. The conservative, contract-preserving choice is to keep `observe`
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:51:as the default and leave `enforce` as an explicit per-project opt-in.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:55:- Strict-DONE coverage stays OFF by default, so a story *can* reach DONE with uncovered
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:56:  milestone rows unless the project opts in. **Mitigation:** observe-mode still renders the
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:57:  gaps as visible (non-blocking) diagnostics, so drift is surfaced, just not blocked.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:58:- A future contributor might read "default observe" as an oversight and flip it.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:59:  **Mitigation:** this decision doc + a code comment at the default site + a regression test
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:60:  pinning the default to `observe`.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:61:- Per-trigger gate-mode selection ("enforce only for milestone-triggered stories") is a
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:62:  legitimate future capability but a separate build, not a config default. **It is
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:63:  explicitly deferred to a future story**, not silently dropped.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:64:- This decision governs only the DEFAULT. Projects that have already set
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:65:  `doneGateMode: "enforce"` keep it — no regression.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:67:## Verification
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:69:A committed regression test pins the config default to `observe` when unset, so a future
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:70:accidental flip is caught. It exercises the **real** resolver
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:71:`configuredProofStoryMode` (`packages/main/src/handlers/phase-gates.ts`,
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:72:`return loadConfig(ctx.root).proofStory?.[key] ?? 'observe';`) against a fresh temp root
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:73:with no `lattice.config.json`, asserting both `doneGateMode` and `reviewGateMode` resolve
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:74:to `observe`. Because the test drives the shipped resolver (not a re-implemented default),
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:75:flipping the `?? 'observe'` fallback to `?? 'enforce'` makes it fail.
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:77:Test location: `packages/main/src/tasks/milestone-done-gate-reconciliation-smoke.ts`,
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:78:block "(c) gate-mode DEFAULT pins to 'observe' when config is unset". (See CHK-009
docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md:79:verification intent.)
